issues.description: The PersonResource implementation in the solution repository has a constructor that takes a NoteService and sets the personService field to null. This conflicts with the template and the problem description which expect PersonResource to receive a PersonService via constructor injection. The incorrect constructor signature and assignment in the solution will prevent proper wiring of PersonService, cause runtime errors (NPEs) and confuse students comparing template and solution.

The PersonResource constructor in the solution repository incorrectly uses a NoteService parameter and sets personService to null, while the template (and the intended design) expect a PersonService to be injected. This renaming/mis-typing breaks the conceptual mapping between the REST resource and the service that implements person-related business logic and will confuse students comparing template, problem statement, and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution, change the PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the personService field (e.g., public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). Ensure the constructor parameter type/name matches the intended PersonService injection.
